name: Bina Chhabria
forbes_bio: Bina Chhabria is chairperson of Allied Blenders and Distillers, India's third largest spirits company by sales volume.
The Mumbai-based company has 33 manufacturing plants and one distillery
Allied has 17 brands across whiskey, rum, gin and vodka. It's best-selling product is Officer's Choice whiskey
Her husband Kishore founded the company in 1988. Their daughter Resham is vice chairperson of Allied Blenders

name: Holger Loclair
forbes_bio: Holger Loclair, originally from the GDR (former socialist East Germany) started working in 1987 at an industrial company that was later named Orafol when capitalism took hold.
West German investor Klaus Schmidbaur owned Orafol until he gradually transferred 99% of it to Loclair during 2013-2016.
Orafol is the world market leader for self-adhesive reflective films and industrial tapes.
Loclair is the only billionaire form former East Germany. His son Christian Loclair invests in startups.

name: Wang Jianguo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2024)
forbes_bio: Wang Jianguo chairs two publicly traded e-commerce businesses he founded in China: Kidswant and Huitongda Network.
Wang holds an EMBA from Australian National University and a Ph.D. in business from Arizona State University.
Wang worked in the commerce department in China's Jiangsu province early in his career.

name: Alberto Coppel Luken
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Alberto Coppel Luken and his four brothers own the family's retailing and banking giant, Grupo Coppel.
Their father and grandfather started the company in 1941 as a small shop in Sinaloa called "El Regalo."
Coppel is the CEO and chairman of GC1 Holding; owner of sake producer Nami and software company ClickBalance.
GC1 Holding's venture capital arm had investments in Spotify, Uber and Pinterest before they went public.
Coppel, who was previously director of stores in the Coppel Group, is a civil engineer with a degree from the Monterrey Institute of Technology.
forbes_facts: He is the vice president of Pronatura Noroeste, a conservation organization in Northwest Mexico.

name: Jeff Lawson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Jeff Lawson is a cofounder of Twilio, a cloud communications platform that adds messaging, voice and video to web and mobile apps.
Lawson launched his first Internet startup while he was at the University of Michigan and went on to become the first CTO of ticket reseller StubHub.
The serial entrepreneur went on to work at Amazon, where he helped build the technology behind Amazon Web Services.
Along with two friends, Lawson started Twilio in 2008 then took it public in 2016.
He stepped down as CEO and and left the company's board in 2024.
forbes_facts: In 2024, Lawson acquired the satirical news site The Onion.
Twilio's first customer was PhoneMyPhone.com, which allowed people to type their numbers into a website to ring their own cellphones.

name: Rodolfo Villela Marino
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Rodolfo Villela Marino is a member of a storied Brazilian banking dynasty.
He is a grandson of Eudoro Libânio Villela, who cofounded Brazilian bank Itau in 1945; it merged with Unibanco in 2008.
Rodolfo Villela Marino sits on the board and serves executive vice president of Itausa, the parent of Itau Unibanco.
His mother, Maria de Lourdes Egydio Villela, a former billionaire, transferred her shares of Itausa to Rodolfo and his brother Ricardo.
He has a degree in business and a doctorate in management from the Getúlio Vargas Foundation (FGV) in São Paulo.
forbes_facts: Villela has a degree in business and a doctorate in management from the Getúlio Vargas Foundation (FGV) in São Paulo.

name: Onkar Kanwar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Onkar Kanwar is chairman of Apollo Tyres which makes tires for cars, trucks, farm vehicles and two-wheelers.
It sells under the Apollo and Vredestein brands in India, Europe and Asia.
He took control of the company in 2002 after a public battle with his father, the late Raunaq Singh, who started the company in 1976.
Neeraj Kanwar, the younger of his two sons, is vice-chairman and managing director.
forbes_facts: The company's Vredestein brand supplies tires for luxury cars.
He enjoys learning about modern management practices and applying them to his business

name: Yuan Zhongxue
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Yang Jianliang is a founder and honorary chairman of Sailun Group, a Chinese tire manufacturer. He stepped down as chairman in July 2021.
Sailun is headquartered in the eastern port city of Qingdao.
Sailun went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Hans-Otto Kromberg
forbes_bio: Hans-Otto Kromberg owns Kromberg & Schubert, a family-owned German maker of cable and wiring.
The company was founded in 1902 by Paul Kromberg and Enrst Schubert, with Kromberg becoming sole owner 12 years later.
Hans-Otto Kromberg took control of his grandfather's company business at age 30 with the goal of expanding into international markets.
Kromberg & Schubert had revenue of 2.7 billion euros, according to its most recent financial filings.

name: Shin Chang-jae
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2024); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Shin Chang-Jae is the chairman and CEO of Kyobo Life Insurance, founded by his father in 1958 as Daehan Kyoyuk Insurance.
When Shin assumed the posts in 2000, Kyobo was reeling from investment portfolio losses in the aftermath of the Asian financial crisis.
He turned the company around, focusing on customer satisfaction and risk control.
With a network of agents and financial planners, the company now offers insurance and asset-management products to more than 5 million customers.
forbes_facts: He has a mischievous penchant for staging stunts to make a point, such as reportedly taking part in his own fake funeral.
In 2010, he received the 19th Montblanc de la Culture Arts Patronage Award for his support of Korean literature through the Daesan Foundation.
